root_cause.text: The IMA securityfs measurement-list creation code in `create_securityfs_measurement_lists()` assumed every TPM bank `crypto_id` was a valid `enum hash_algo` and indexed `hash_algo_name[]` with it, even though unsupported TPM algorithms are represented by the sentinel `HASH_ALGO__LAST`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states `ima_tpm_chip->allocated_banks[i].crypto_id is initialized to HASH_ALGO__LAST if the TPM algorithm is not supported`, yet the old code directly used `hash_algo_name[algo]`; the patch adds an explicit `if (algo == HASH_ALGO__LAST)` path and uses `alg_id`-based filenames instead, fixing the reported KASAN global out-of-bounds in `hash_algo_name`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix securityfs measurement file naming for TPM algorithms without a standard hash_algo_name by falling back to TPM algorithm ID-based names.
intent_record.what: The code in create_securityfs_measurement_lists() was changed to conditionally format securityfs file names based on the hash algorithm: when algo equals HASH_ALGO__LAST, it now uses sprintf() to build ascii and binary measurement file names with a "tpm_alg_%x" suffix derived from ima_tpm_chip->allocated_banks[i].alg_id; otherwise it keeps the existing names based on hash_algo_name[algo].
intent_record.how: At runtime, this allows measurement list files to be created for TPM banks whose algorithm does not map to a known hash_algo_name entry, avoiding use of the normal name array for the HASH_ALGO__LAST sentinel and instead generating a valid fallback name from the TPM algorithm ID.

grouping_result.intent: Fix securityfs measurement file naming for TPM algorithms without a standard hash_algo_name by falling back to TPM algorithm ID-based names.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the faulty assumption that every TPM bank crypto_id maps to a valid hash_algo_name entry. By adding a fallback for TPM algorithms without a standard hash_algo_name, it avoids relying on invalid enum-based indexing and is therefore tied to the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This directly indexes hash_algo_name[] with algo, assuming it is a valid enum hash_algo. When unsupported TPM algorithms map to HASH_ALGO__LAST, this can access the array out of bounds or use an invalid entry.
The same unsafe array indexing is repeated for the binary measurement file name path, again assuming every TPM bank crypto_id has a valid hash_algo_name[] entry.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement indexes hash_algo_name[] using algo under the assumption that every TPM bank crypto_id maps to a valid enum hash_algo. For unsupported TPM algorithms, algo can be HASH_ALGO__LAST, making this an invalid array index and the root cause of the vulnerability.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full newly added `create_securityfs_measurement_lists()` logic where the vulnerable indexing occurs. In that function, the code does `algo = ima_algo_array[i].algo;` and then immediately uses it as an index in `hash_algo_name[algo]` twice: `sprintf(file_name, "ascii_runtime_measurements_%s", hash_algo_name[algo]);` and `sprintf(file_name, "binary_runtime_measurements_%s", hash_algo_name[algo]);`. The root cause says the code wrongly assumes every TPM bank `crypto_id` / mapped algorithm is a valid `enum hash_algo`, while unsupported TPM algorithms are represented by the sentinel `HASH_ALGO__LAST`. There is no validation here that `algo` is within the valid range before indexing `hash_algo_name[]`. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present. The fix is not present because there is no bounds check, no filtering of unsupported banks, and no special handling for the sentinel value before dereferencing `hash_algo_name[algo]`.
